title: Phased warm-standby priming with tier-aware routing and variant fallback orchestration
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Background: Our smart routing stack needs a coordinated mechanism to bring standby regions online that minimizes cold starts, avoids thundering herd behavior on model variants, and preserves latency SLOs for P0 customers. Current warm-standby priming probes are independent per-region and do not consider multi-tier routing rules or model-variant compatibility, which leads to uneven cache saturation and occasional capacity storms during large-scale cutovers.

Goal: Implement a phased warm-standby priming orchestrator that: (1) primes KV cache and model weights in prioritized phases using demand-shaping signals; (2) integrates tier-aware routing so that traffic ramps respect customer SLAs and reserved capacity pools; (3) coordinates fallback model variant pre-warm when primary variants are not available in the target region; (4) exposes readiness scores to Console and the routing policy engine for automated cutovers.

Scope: Orchestrator service plus runtime hooks, a readiness scoring model, CLI/operator runbooks, and Console telemetry. Includes integration tests and a staged rollout plan.

Out of scope: New autoscaling policies for Dedicated pools (we will surface suggestions but not change scalers here), and on-prem packaging for air-gapped installs (follow-up work).
acceptance_criteria: Orchestrator can execute phased priming plans across at least three regions and three routing tiers in staging with synthetic traffic
Readiness score (0-100) correlates with KV cache hit rate, model weight load status, and per-model cold-start latency; documented mapping between metric thresholds and readiness levels
Routing policy engine accepts readiness signals and defers traffic routing if region readiness < configured threshold for a tier
Fallback variant pre-warm launches and completes within configured window when chosen variant differs from primary; system falls back safely if variant pre-warm fails
Console dashboard surfaces per-region readiness, priming phase, kv-saturation histogram, and last priming run logs
Automated chaos test that kills a region during priming demonstrates graceful rollback and no global SLO violation beyond defined guardrails
tasks: Design: define priming phases, signals, and readiness formula (Ava + Research)
Runtime: add priming plug-points to deployment agent to accept phased directives (Liam)
Routing: modify smart router to consume readiness signals and implement tier delay/backoff rules (Sanjay)
Variants: implement deterministic pre-warm DAG for fallback model variants with dependency ordering (Priya)
Observability: expose KV cache heatmaps, weight load progress, and readiness trace (Maya)
E2E tests: synthetic traffic harness for phased ramp and chaos scenarios (QA)
Runbook: operator runbook for manual intervention and emergency abort (Ops)

notes: 2025-02-18 - Ava Martinez: Initial ticket created after on-call postmortem where two regional cutovers caused KV cache hot spots and an availability blip for high-tier customers.

2025-02-21 - Design review: agreed to use a phased 3-stage priming model (seed, ramp, verify) with exponential token-prefix shadowing to reduce thundering herd; decided to surface a single numeric readiness score per region and per model variant.

2025-02-25 - Engineering sync: runtime agent will expose a /priming status endpoint; orchestrator will push directives over existing control channel; fallback variant pre-warm will reuse existing model-loader code with added DAG ordering and timeout semantics.

2025-02-27 - Trade-off: aggressive priming improves latency but increases cross-region egress cost; decided on configurable priming budget per namespace and a conservative default to mitigate costs for free-tier customers.

2025-03-01 - PR #4219 merged to add agent hooks; integration tests for seed and ramp phases passing in staging. Noted flakiness under heavy synthetic traffic—investigating router backoff policy tuning.
2025-03-02 - Router PR pending additional metrics; plan to add kv-saturation hysteresis to avoid flip-flopping readiness during transient load spikes.
